prompts.text: Have a helper go through every file in src and list anything that looks like dead code, while I keep working on the README with you.
Spin up two helpers: one to review src/parse.ts for edge-case bugs, and the other to review src/format.ts for the same. Report back with both findings together.
Can you get a helper to search the whole project for every place we read from process.env or process.argv? I want a tidy list with file and line.
delegate a side task: have a helper draft a CHANGELOG entry from the current state of package.json and the README, and don't let it touch any source files
I'd like a helper to audit package.json for outdated or unnecessary dependencies and scripts while you carry on explaining the CLI entry point to me.
Send a helper off to hunt through all three source files for inconsistent error handling. Meanwhile I'll wait; just summarize what it finds.
Two helpers please, in parallel. First one checks that every claim in the README matches what src/cli.ts actually does. Second one checks the type annotations across src for anything loose like any.
Hey, could a helper grep the project for TODO, FIXME, and HACK comments and give me a ranked list by how risky they look?
Use a helper to write a rough test plan for the parsing module in the background. I only need bullet points, and I don't want you stopping what you're doing.
Please have a helper trace how data flows from the CLI through parse and into format, and write up the call path step by step so I can onboard a teammate.
get a helper to do a naming consistency sweep over every file: variables, exports, file names. just report, no edits
I want a second pair of eyes that isn't you. Have a helper independently review src/cli.ts for usability problems, and have another helper review the README for gaps a new user would hit.
Could you hand off to a helper the job of checking whether tsconfig strictness settings, if any exist, fit the code in src? Search everything, since I'm not sure where the config lives.
Delegate a scan to a helper: find every import statement across the project and tell me if there are any circular or unused ones.
While we talk through the release plan, have a helper quietly look through all files for hard-coded strings that should be constants or config.
Run a helper over the codebase to collect every exported symbol and which file imports it, then give me the table. Keep it going on its own while I grab coffee.
What's the practical difference between a type and an interface in TypeScript?
I keep getting "Cannot find module" when I run my compiled output, even though the import path looks right in the editor. What usually causes that?
Should I use async/await or promise chains in a tiny CLI like this one? Just pick one and tell me why.
Explain what "strict": true actually turns on in tsconfig, in plain words.
Is it worth adding a linter to a project this small?
why does TS say 'Object is possibly undefined' when I already checked it two lines up
Quick one: ESM or CommonJS for a new Node tool in 2026? I need a recommendation, not a survey.
Briefly, what does a README for a command-line tool need at minimum so a stranger can use it?
Walk me through what happens when Node runs a script with a shebang line at the top and the file has been made executable.
Tradeoffs between throwing errors and returning a result object when parsing bad input? I'm leaning toward throwing but not sure.
Can you tell me what semantic versioning means for going from 0.3.2 to 0.4.0?
Is it bad practice to keep parsing and formatting in separate files when each is only about fifteen lines? Be honest.
What does the "main" versus "bin" field in package.json do, and when do I need each?
Decide for me: tabs or two spaces for this project, and give me one sentence of justification.
I'm confused about unknown versus any. When would I reach for unknown?
Give me a short, friendly explanation of what a unit test is that I could read to a coworker who has never written one.
